title: Knowledge check: Form Security and Reliability

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of form security and reliability?
options: Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.
Read values with .val(), validate to guide the user, and display actionable errors. Client-side validation never replaces server-side validation or authorization.
Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
questions.answer_key: Read values with .val(), validate to guide the user, and display actionable errors. Client-side validation never replaces server-side validation or authorization.
questions.explanation: Read values with .val(), validate to guide the user, and display actionable errors. Client-side validation never replaces server-side validation or authorization. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying why client-side validation is not sufficient?
options: Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Use why client-side validation is not sufficient deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.answer_key: Use why client-side validation is not sufficient deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with form security and reliability?
options: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
